answer: A concrete sybil defence is time-locked proof of work: a fresh identity must wait several epochs and burn growing compute before it can be graded, so a fleet costs real wall-clock time rather than free keys. Naming an nebula of fresh keys, a trellis of shared metadata, or a spiral of repeated phrasing makes the farm visible, and its marginal cost per fake identity grows instead of staying flat, so mass identity farming stops paying.
